title: When both of us agree
odia: ତୋର ମୋର ରାଜି, କିସ କରିବ କାଜି
literal_meaning: You and I agree—what can the qazi do?
explanation: The rhyme between raji and qazi turns agreement into a cheeky challenge to an outside authority. The dictionary places it under the qazi’s marriage-registration role. Its force is rhetorical: if the people concerned agree, why should someone else obstruct them? That is the speaker’s claim, not a statement that consent removes legal duties.
meaning_odia: ତୁ ରାଜି, ମୁଁ ରାଜି—ତେବେ ମଝିରେ ଆଉ କାହାର ବାଧା କାହିଁକି? ରାଜି ଓ କାଜିର ମିଳ ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନକୁ ଟିକେ ମଜା ଓ ଟିକେ ଆହ୍ୱାନର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ କାଜିଙ୍କ ବିବାହ ପଞ୍ଜୀକରଣ ଭୂମିକା ପାଖରେ ଏହି ଉଦାହରଣ ଅଛି। ଏହା କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ଯୁକ୍ତି; ଆଇନର ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: The rhyme between raji and qazi turns agreement into a cheeky challenge to an outside authority.

usage_example: Two collaborators agree on a meeting time while an uninvolved acquaintance keeps objecting; one jokingly uses the saying. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
